evidence: In situ quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) and in situ FTIR vibrational spectroscopy. Set of ex situ characterization techniques are employed to study the material properties. As deposited NiS films on fluorine doped tin oxide (FTO) glass were subjected to cyclic voltammetry measurements in I-/I3- electrolyte to study its electrochemical activity in comparison to the Pt metal electrode. The crystallinity of the as deposited NiS thin film was characterized by grazing angle x-ray diffraction (XRD) as well as transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectroscopy (TOFSIMS) measurements were investigated to study elemental composition and various isotopes of all the elements present throughout ALD grown NiS films on soda lime glass. Temperature dependent Hall measurements under van der Pauw configuration were carried out to study electrical properties such as resistivity, carrier concentration, and mobility of NiS versus temperature. Cyclic voltammograms (CVs) were captured using a computer controlled potentiostat (Autolab) in a three electrode configuration using I-/I3- electrolyte. The analysis gun raster size was 60 x 60 lm while 600 x 600 lm was the sputtering crater size selected for acquisition of depth profile with 2 s sputter rate (slow sputtering) and 6 analysis frames per cycle. The cocentric diffraction fringes [Fig. 10(a)] confirm the crystalline nature of as deposited films perceived from XRD analysis. The diffraction peaks suggest the formation of polycrystalline rhombohedral NiS (b-NiS, JCPDS card No. 12-0041) without any preferred orientation. The resistivity, mobility, and bulk carrier concentration are measured within the temperature range of 18–300 K. The electrochemical activity of the as deposited NiS is investigated by cyclic voltammetry in I-/I3- electrolyte under three-electrode system. The as obtained depth profiles are shown in Fig. 11. It clearly indicates the presence of Ni and S elements throughout the film without any oxygen count above the detectable limit. The redox pair at relatively negative potentials (on the left) corresponds to reduction of I3- to I- as dictated in Eq. (4), which directly affects the DSSC performance. The redox peaks at relatively positive potentials (right side redox pairs) correspond to redox reaction as explained in Eq. (5). The electrochemical stability test in I-/I3- redox electrolyte is performed. The authors also thank Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility at IIT Bombay for material characterizations.
